title: Handoff handshake protocol for cross-team canaries (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This scratchpad defines a lightweight, repeatable "handshake" protocol for cross-team canaries. Goal is to reduce friction at the moment of activation and make human gates explicit, timeboxed, and reversible.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to staged activations where multiple teams (product, serving-runtime, infra, SRE, customer success) must coordinate.
- Not for emergency hotfix rollouts (those use emergency stop/runbook in SRE playbook).
- We assume traffic slicing tooling already supports weighted routing, dynamic rollback, and telemetry tagging.

Quick failure modes we want to defend against (notes):
- Latency shock across a cohort due to model size mismatch (e.g., large->large variant routed by mistake).
- Split contamination (A/B assignment leaking to control cohort).
- Cost runaway: aggressive model variant increases token cost and triggers budget alarms later.
- Behavioral regression: hallucination or policy regression detected by human reviewers.

The Handshake protocol (3-phase, timeboxed):
1) PREP (T-48 to T-1 hours) — asynchronous checks
   - Owners: feature PM (initiator), SRE (infra readiness), runtime eng (model plumbing)
   - Artifacts to attach to handshake message: hypothesis one-liner, target cohorts, traffic schedule, guardrail metrics, synthetic probe plan, rollback criteria, test-run links (staging traces), runbook contact list.
   - Checklist (hand-off):
     - IRL smoke script exists and passes in staging (link to github action).
     - Probe coverage: latency p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, error rates, safety score from eval harness all within threshold.
     - Capacity cushion verified: dedicated pool headroom >= 25% or autoscale policy configured.

2) GO WINDOW (T=0) — synchronous small-batch activation
   - Owners: rollout steward (operator), serving-runtime oncall, PM observer, SRE oncall.
   - Activation steps:
     - Activate slice with 0.5% traffic for 10 minutes OR 1000 requests, whichever comes first.
     - Run synthetic probe spike concurrently targeting the same path for controlled load sample.
     - Human review checklist executed at T+5m and T+10m: quick pass/fail on latency, error spikes, and top-3 behavioral flags.
   - Quick Slack template (to post in #rollout-coordinator):
     - "GO WINDOW: {feature} enabled on slice {id} at {time}. Steward: @{steward}. Monitoring probe: {link}. Please ack in 5m."

3) SCALE (T+small window) — gradual ramp or canary expansion
   - If GO WINDOW passes, steward ramps per schedule (0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50%) with 30–60 minute holds.
   - At each hold: automated checks + 2 human glance checks (PM and SRE) before moving to next.
   - If any metric breaches rollback threshold, steward immediately cuts traffic to previous stable route and triggers postmortem cadence.

Decision heuristics (simple):
- AUTOMATED FAIL if: p99 latency > baseline * 2 OR error-rate > baseline + 0.5% absolute OR safety-score drop > 5 points.
- HUMAN BLOCK if: multiple human reviewers flag behavioral regressions (2 independent reviewers) OR customer success flags escalations from early customers.
- COST PAUSE if estimated cost increase > 15% week-over-week on the canary cohort and finance/PM are not aligned.

Roles & responsibilities (short):
- Steward: coordinates the handshake, executes activation steps, posts Slack updates, triggers rollback.
- Runtime Eng: ensures model variant mapping and KV cache warmup strategy.
- SRE/Infra: confirms capacity, circuit-breakers, global routing safety.
- PM: validates hypothesis, watches UX signals, coordinates comms.
- CS/Legal (optional): fast consult if the canary touches regulated customers.

Example concrete timeline (template to copy):
- T-48h: Prep artifacts posted, SRE + runtime ack.
- T-2h: Dry run on staging, smoke test results attached.
- T-30m: Pre-flight Slack ping to org + 2-person on-call roster.
- T=0: GO WINDOW (0.5% for 10m).
- T+15m: Inspect probes. If pass -> ramp to 2% for 30m.
- T+45m: Inspect -> ramp to 10% for 60m.
- T+2h: Inspect -> ramp to 50% then monitor 4h before global.

Metric checklist (minimum):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 vs baseline
- Error rate (5xx/timeout) absolute and relative
- Customer-facing SLA violations (if any)
- Safety/regression score from evals and human-review flags
- Cost extrapolation (per-1k token math + estimated QPS)
- Trace sampling for root-cause linking (link to tracing dashboard)

Escalation ladder (contact order):
- Steward -> Runtime Eng -> SRE oncall -> Eng Director -> Incident Commander (if > 30m unresolved and customer impact)

Sample rollback message (short):
- "ROLLBACK: {feature} slice {id} cut at {time}. Reason: p99 spike / safety regression. Steward: @{steward}. All traffic routed to stable-{tag}. Postmortem owner: @{owner}."

Open questions / TODOs (to resolve in next sync):
- How do we handle overlapping canaries where two features share user cohorts? Need deconflict algorithm (priority, tie-breaker).
- Do we want a small web UI button for steward to ‘pause & collect trace’ rather than full rollback? (UX / security implications).
- Concrete thresholds: should they be absolute (easier) or relative (more flexible)? Create a threshold matrix per product-line.
- Should CS customers be auto-opted-out of early canaries unless whitelisted? (privacy/regulatory).

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Consider a micro-signer step: small signed ack from two people (steward + SRE) to unblock GO WINDOW.
- Add an automated canary-run summary email to stakeholders at end of Scale stage with 1-line verdict + link to artifacts.
- Build a small script to compute estimated cost delta for a given ramp schedule (input: QPS, token/sample, model multiplier).

Related artifacts / quick links:
- Confluence: rollout-playbook (linked above)
- Example: github actions smoke-run (link above)
- JIRA: JIRA-1128 (tracking the handshake feature RSVP)

If you want to iterate: please add comments inline below or drop quick PR to the rollout-sim repo with simulation scenarios for overlapping cohorts.

-- Maya
